title: Relative perfection of algebraic upper shriek for flat Noetherian algebras
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finite type homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-flat-morphism]. For any polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$, set $K=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)[n]\in D(A)$, with the $A$-module structure of derived coinduction [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$, meaning that it is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]; it has bounded finitely generated cohomology; and it has finite Tor amplitude over $R$, meaning that there are integers $a\le b$ such that $H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for all $R$-modules $M$ and all $i\notin[a,b]$. Moreover, the scalar map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,K)$ is an isomorphism. No local complete-intersection hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

proof.text: Because $R\to A$ is flat and of finite type over Noetherian rings, the flat-finite-presentation-perfect theorem makes it a perfect ring map; the polynomial presentation $P\twoheadrightarrow A$ then makes $A$ a perfect $P$-complex with a bounded finite-projective resolution.

proof.text: Apply bounded coherent upper shriek to $R[0]$, which has its only cohomology the cyclic module $R$. Step 1 verifies that $A$ is perfect over the chosen polynomial presentation. The polynomial model of [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-calculus] identifies this upper-shriek object with $K=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)[n]$, with its natural $A$-action. Thus $K$ has bounded finitely generated cohomology over $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] to the Noetherian ring $A$: boundedness supplies its upper cohomology bound and each cohomology module is finite, so $K$ is pseudo-coherent, represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules.

proof.text: By Step 1, $A$ is a perfect $P$-complex. Perfect-complex derived biduality makes $D=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)$ perfect, so choose a bounded finite-projective $P$-complex $E$ representing it. Each term is a direct summand of a finite free $P$-module, and hence is $R$-flat: $P$ has its monomial basis over $R$, direct sums of copies of $R$ preserve injections under tensor, and the same holds for a direct summand. If $E$ is supported in degrees $[u,v]$, its shifted bounded flat model computes $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M=E[n]\otimes_R M$ for every $R$-module $M$ and vanishes outside $[u-n,v-n]$. This gives one finite Tor interval independent of $M$.

source.place: Tag 0BZW, lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic, part (1)(b), using More on Algebra Tag 07VI.

proof.text:
Put $D=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)\in D(A)$ with its coinduced action, so $K=D[n]$. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] to $P\to A$ with $X=D[n]$ and $Y=P[n]$. After restriction of scalars it gives
$$U R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,K)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_P(UD[n],P[n])\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_P(R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P),P).$$
The same node identifies the transported scalar-action map with the canonical double-dual evaluation $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_P(R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P),P)$; this is the compatibility $a\mapsto(h\mapsto h(a))$, not merely an isomorphism of the two objects. Since Step 1 made $A$ perfect over $P$, [lem-trf-perfect-complex-derived-biduality] makes this evaluation map an isomorphism. Restriction of scalars reflects isomorphisms: the cohomology of the cone has exactly the same underlying groups before and after restriction. The original scalar map is therefore an isomorphism in $D(A)$.

lean.statement: theorem algebraicShriek_relative_perfect {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] [HasDerivedCategory.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] (φ : R →+* A) (hflat : RingHom.Flat φ) (hfinite : RingHom.FiniteType φ) (n : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →+* A) (hp : Function.Surjective p) (hcomp : p.comp (MvPolynomial.C : R →+* MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) = φ) : DerivedCategory.IsPseudoCoherent (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (algebraicShriekPolynomialComplex n p)) ∧ (∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (algebraicShriekPolynomialComplex n p)))) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (algebraicShriekPolynomialComplex n p)))) ∧ (∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u} R) a b ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapDerivedCategory.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (algebraicShriekPolynomialComplex n p)))) ∧ IsIso (algebraicShriekScalarMap (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (algebraicShriekPolynomialComplex n p)))
